content_of_post_to_answer: Why might I feel resistant to trying new coping strategies, and how can I overcome this?
answer: Resistance to new coping strategies is often less about laziness and more about protection: familiar struggles can feel safer than unfamiliar solutions. A new strategy asks you to trust a process before you have proof it works, which creates discomfort. I've explored this pattern in more detail on my profile for anyone wanting to go deeper. Real change often begins when we stop asking “why can’t I do this?” and ask “what is this resistance trying to protect?”
